THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR HEARING ON 06.10.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 M.A.C.A.No.37 of 2020  3  2025:KER:73669  C.S.SUDHA, J.

 Dated this the 6th day of October 2025  JUDGMENT

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P. (MV) No.1894/2012 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Thrissur (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 03/05/2019.
The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 24/06/2012 at 03:00 p.m., while she was riding scooter bearing registration no.KL-45-G-8208 through Puthur-Kuttanellur road and when she reached near Kalady bus stop, autorickshaw bearing registration no.KL-8/3658 driven by the second respondent in a 2025:KER:73669 rash and negligent manner knocked her down, as a result of which she sustained grievous injuries.

sentences.text: The first respondent/owner, second respondent/driver and fourth respondent-insured of the offending autorickshaw remained ex-parte.
4. The third respondent-insurer filed written statement admitting the policy.
It was contended that the claim petitioner and the second respondent had no driving license at the time of the accident.
The averments in the petition regarding age, income and occupation of the claim petitioner were disputed.
The compensation claimed under various heads was contended to be exorbitant.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A13 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
Exts.B1 and B2 were marked on the side of the respondents.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found 2025:KER:73669 negligence on the part of the second respondent-driver of the offending autorickshaw resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 1,61,500/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

8. Heard both sides.
9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner- Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter, a tailor was earning 7,500/- per month.

However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 5,000/-, which is quite low going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v.
2025:KER:73669 Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236.
9.1.

entities.text:
Ramachandrappa v.
2025:KER:73669 Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the light of the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra), the notional income is fixed as 8,500/-
per month.
Loss of earnings 10.
The materials on record show that the claim petitioner sustained the following injuries- " Lacerated wound right ankle, right foot with skin loss and tendons exposed.
Abrasion and contusion both knees left elbow and abrasion nose."
She was hospitalized for a period of 20 days.
In all probability, she might have been unable to work for a period of 6 months.

Hence, she can be awarded compensation for a period of 6 months, that is,
8,500/- x 6 =51,000/-.
Multiplier 11.
The claim petitioner was aged 32 years.

Dhanya vs Manoj on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99827356/
3 2025:KER:73669 Therefore, the correct multiplier is '16' and not 17 as applied by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: The impugned Award shall stand modified to the said extent also.
Percentage of disability 12.

According to the learned counsel for the claim petitioner, when Ext.A11 disability certificate shows that she had sustained 6% whole body disability, the Tribunal was not justified in scaling down the disability to 4%.
According to her, the functional disability also ought to have been fixed at 6%.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that the functional disability that has been fixed is quite reasonable and that it does not call for any interference.
12.1. Ext.A11 certificate was objected to when it was attempted to be brought in evidence and marked.
Despite the same, no steps were taken to examine the doctor who issued the same.
I have already referred to the injury sustained by the claim 2025:KER:73669 petitioner.
The materials on record also show that the claim petitioner has sustained a crush injury on her right leg, which aspect is not disputed.

Therefore, taking into account the avocation of the claim petitioner, that is, a tailor,
this would have affected her functioning or ability as a tailor.
Hence, I find that the functional disability can be fixed as 6% taking into account the nature of the injuries sustained by her.

13. The impugned Award is modified to the following extent:

1. Loss of 30,000/- 25,000/- 51,000/-

2. Medical 40,000/- 54,200/- 54,200/-

3. Bystander 5,000/- 4,000/- 4,000/-
 expenses (No modification)
4. Transportation 3,000/- 2,500/- 2,500/-
 expenses (No modification)
5. Extra 10,000/- 2,000/- 2,000/-
 nourishment (No modification)
6. Damage to 2,000/- 1,000/- 1,000/-
 clothing etc (No modification)
 2025:KER:73669 7. Pain and 20,000/- 20,000/- 20,000/-
 suffering (No modification)
8. Compensation 50,000/- 40,800/- 97,920/-
 for continuing (8,500/- x 12 x 16 x Dhanya vs Manoj on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99827356/
4  or permanent 6%)
 disability 9. Compensation 20,000/- - Nil  for injury itself (No modification)
10. Loss of - 10,000/- 10,000/-
 amenities and (No modification)
 enjoyment in  life 11. Personal - 2,000/- 2,000/-
 assistance (No modification)
12. Future 15,000/- - Nil  treatment (No modification)
 1,95,000/- 1,61,500/- 2,44,620/-
In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 83,120/- (total compensation = 2,44,620/- that is, 1,61,500/- granted by the Tribunal + 83,120/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization (excluding the period of 39 days delay in filing the appeal) and proportionate costs.
The third respondent/
insurer is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On 2025:KER:73669 deposit of the amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
The liberty granted by the Tribunal to the third respondent/insurer to recover the amount from the first respondent/owner is confirmed.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
